title: Consent stamped at write time: a later opt-in never re-labels old data
request: Phase 1's first remaining gap from the owner's capture document: each record stores the consent level it was written under, so a later change of the switches never re-labels old data; adoptable by the main product.
spec: A level on every event and decision at write time; exports keep a record only when its stamp and the switches allow the use; consent changes are events; the rules and contracts in dclab_core, the adapter taking the host's level.
plan: Put the ladder and its rules in dclab_core.
Add the stamp to the two contracts, old versions still read.
Stamp at the studio's two writers from the workspace folder and the project's switches.
Make the exports require the stamp.
Record consent changes; count the record by level on the consent page.
Test, publish the schemas, run the wheel, record, commit.

decisions.decision: An export requires both the stamp and the current switch.
decisions.why: The stamp can only restrict: a withdrawal still blocks everything, and a writer's brief cache can never widen what leaves.

decisions.decision: A writer with no project store reachable stamps the workspace's level; a project the store does not know is operate.
decisions.why: Direct writers (tests, a worker outside a request) cannot read a project; the export checks the project again at export time.

decisions.decision: A switch change is written under the level it brings in.
decisions.why: It is the first record of that level, and the history of consent stands beside what it governs.

decisions.decision: A project's record written where no store can be read is operate.
decisions.why: The stamp promises the level at write time; a guess from the workspace alone could be higher than the project allowed.

change: dclab_core consent.py (new), experience.py, ledger.py, adapters/main_product_experience.py, schemas, CHANGELOG (0.38.0); dclab_rnd consent.py, experience, ledger, pages/consent.py, routers/projects.py; tests consent, core_experience, ledger, datasets; CORE_INTEGRATION.md, EXPERIENCE_ARCHIVE.md, the plan.

findings.defect: Records written by tests before the switches were turned on stopped leaving.
findings.scenario: Four dataset tests and three export tests built nothing.
findings.cause: The new rule itself: a record carries the level at its write.
findings.fix: The tests give consent before they write, and withdraw both uses where every set must go.

findings.defect: A writer outside a request stamped every project record operate.
findings.scenario: Decisions written straight to a ledger never left, and on PostgreSQL the folder was unknown.
findings.cause: No project store is reachable outside a request, and the PostgreSQL stores carried no folder.
findings.fix: No store means the workspace's level; the stores learn their folder when opened.

findings.defect: The main product's adapter did not list the new kind.
findings.scenario: The conformance test found a contract kind neither produced nor explained.
findings.cause: A new kind without its reason.
findings.fix: consent.changed listed as missing with the reason.

findings.defect: A route test's audit rows reached another test's count.
findings.scenario: The switches-off test counted one more set_consent row.
findings.fix: The route test has its own app.

findings.defect: A test pinned the event contract's old version.
findings.scenario: The lineage test failed on v3.

findings.defect: The catalog did not show rows per level.
findings.scenario: The done-when's last clause was not met.
findings.fix: The manifest (v2) counts each row's stamp, the builders stamp their rows with the lowest level of their sources, the catalog prints it.

findings.defect: A worker's cache could stamp above the switch for ten seconds, and the legacy opt-in moved the train switch unrecorded.
findings.scenario: A project opted out mid-run kept train stamps for ten seconds; share_for_training changed the level with no event and no invalidation.
findings.cause: The API's invalidation never reaches a worker process; the legacy branch sat beside the consent branch.
findings.fix: The standalone worker reads a project's switches each time; the legacy switch is recorded and invalidated like a consent change.

findings.defect: A writer with no services stamped a project's record at the workspace level.
findings.scenario: A script writing with a project id stamped train for a project whose switch was off.
findings.cause: The no-store fallback trusted the workspace alone.
findings.fix: The writer opens the folder's stores; a project it cannot read is operate.

findings.defect: Operate-stamped events shaped the failure signals.
findings.scenario: Events written before an opt-in fed the failures set.
findings.cause: The session filter checked the switch only.
findings.fix: The stamp is checked there too.

findings.defect: The workspace cache keyed on the mtime alone and was never cleared.
findings.scenario: Two changes within the clock's resolution left a stale level.
findings.fix: Keyed on mtime_ns and size; invalidate clears it.

findings.defect: The consent page parsed the newest two hundred thousand events on every load.
findings.scenario: Seconds per page on PostgreSQL and partial counts.
findings.fix: One grouped query on PostgreSQL; the whole record on files.

findings.defect: The legacy opt-in wrote a second audit row.
findings.scenario: The audit's wiring test found two policy rows after one change of share_for_training.
findings.cause: The legacy switch was routed through the consent branch, which audits its own row.
findings.fix: The legacy switch keeps its one audit row; the record gets the consent.changed event and the writers are invalidated.

measurements.name: the stamp holds
measurements.gate: an event written at operate never enters a dataset after the workspace opts in
measurements.result: of two events and two decisions, the ones written at operate stay home after both switches are turned on; the record counts one operate and one train
limits: File stores in the test; PostgreSQL stores through the same writer.

outcome: Every record carries the level it was written under; a later opt-in widens nothing; the main product takes the level from its settings through the adapter.
lessons: A rule about write time changes every test that wrote first and consented later: that is the rule working.
A store opened by a writer must know its folder, or the writer cannot read the switches.
risks: A project switch changed through the API reaches a worker's cache within ten seconds; until then its stamp can be higher than the new level, which the export's own check covers.
